correctness.rationale: All six epoch maps were derived from the actual three-step composition. A common contraction gives existence and uniqueness of the invariant law. The ordered normalized digit gaps are exactly q, 1-q, 2q, 1-q, q. Their comparison with the interval-image length gives a strictly decreasing quartic disjointness frontier and strictly decreasing cubic full-support frontier. The central gap is explicitly positive if and only if the cubic is positive. The full-interval sufficiency uses covering plus IFS uniqueness, and the dimension formula is restricted to strong separation. Eight rational parameter systems with exact finite-epoch moment checks passed the standalone portable checker; finite checks were not used in place of universal proof.

value.rationale: The smallest three-component symmetric permutation example produces six distinct epoch maps and two independent digit-gap scales. The exact interval-support iff threshold and distinct exact first-generation disjointness threshold describe a meaningful learning-rate phase diagram for stationary uncertainty under random reshuffling, with an explicit persistent central gap and a rigorously parameterized Cantor dimension regime. This is a motivated complete interval-covering classification rather than a renamed generic IFS theorem, a new convergence-rate claim, or a variance-table recomputation.
